title: Chapter Five
collection: The Life of St Andrew the Fool

sections.heading: Chapter Five — up through the heavens to the throne

pairs.en: *The account of the same ecstasy, and of the things he saw, continued.*

**35.** *While I stood there shuddering with awe, out of my senses at the strangeness of the thing, turning over in my mind how such a good had come to me, that third wind also died away, and all at once there was the deepest stillness.*

*So I went on a little, to cross that river, and came out on the wide plain of that divine garden; and I looked at its measureless breadth, which God, who can do all things, had made rich with delight upon delight.* *And truly, though I long to set out the riches of the Lord to your love, it does not come into my mind how a human tongue is to do it.*

*When I had come, as I said, to that level ground, and stood looking at the Holy of Holies, behold, another wind blew from the north with a fragrance most delightful, such as roses and lilies scatter, and with a purple colour of the kind that is in violets.* *At this the plants began to ripple again and gave off a scent finer than any ointment or musk, and it went through into my inmost parts.*

*By what sort of eyes I came to all this, bodily or spiritual, God knows.* *To myself I certainly seemed to be there in the body.* *But afterwards, when I felt in my body none of the usual weight, and no desire to look at anything, and none of the other things that press our tent down in this present life, another thought came into my mind: that it was outside the body that I had enjoyed those delights.* *Whether that is so, God knows, who sees into the inward parts of the heart.*

*Then, as those thick-standing plants were stirred in that wonderful way by the coming of the fourth wind, and gave out a sound, and drew the sweetest music out of it, once again the surpassing excellence of the fragrance struck me, and a marvellous sweetness came in through the organs of smell and threw my mind into astonishment.* *So I stood there out of my senses, and within I was flooded with a hidden light.*

**36.** *Enjoying these things I was filled with great gladness; my soul leapt and my spirit exulted.* *And when the fourth wind too had dropped, I observed a very great and wonderful thing: in all the time I spent there no night ever fell, but one unbroken day shone without any turning; and whatever I looked at was joy and life and splendour and gladness without measure.*

*After this I was caught out of my senses into ecstasy, and I seemed to myself to be standing above the firmament of heaven.* *And I thought that a young man in a fine cloak, his face shining like the sun — and I supposed him to be none other than the one who had struck me across the face with the flowering branch when I was failing from the cold — was going before me as my guide, and giving orders to his servants to carry me elsewhere.*

*So with him leading me, behold, there met us a cross of immense size, beautiful to look at, like the rainbow when it stands in the cloud, with four veils drawn round about it like a shining cloud: two of them flashed fiery, no differently from lightning, and the other two yielded nothing to snow in whiteness.* *Singers stood about the cross, beautiful, tall of stature, bright as light, striking out the most fiery rays from their eyes; and they drew out the sweetest harmony in honour of the Crucified.*

*And when my cloaked guide passed that way, he did reverence and greeted the cross, and with a nod showed me to do the same; and I did so, following my guide's example, and at once I felt myself filled with a sweetness like honey, and refreshed by such a fragrance as I had not smelt even in that most fragrant garden.*

*Then, turning my eyes downward, I found beneath us what looked like the deep of the sea, and I began to shake in every limb, and to be afraid that I might fall headlong into it.* *So I called out to my guide and said: “My lord, my leader, see, I am walking as it were on the clouds, and a great fear has taken hold of me.* *I am afraid — even though I tread lightly — that they will not be able to carry me, and that I shall fall from here and be swept down into the waters below.”*

**37.** *To this my guide answered me: “Do not be afraid of anything; we have to climb higher still.”* *And with that he stretched out his hand to me, and we were lifted above a second heaven, and the look of it was snow-white.*

*Here too I saw two crosses, very like the one I had venerated in the heaven below; and these also were ringed, as the first had been, by a holy company singing sweetly; and the air there shone like fire, and the beautiful spirits who lived in that place enjoyed the deepest peace.* *So we venerated these crosses too, as we had the first, with a longing and a love beyond the common; and the fragrance that came off them was plainly divine, and cannot be put into words, so that I was flooded with a far greater delight than from the other cross.*

*I looked away in another direction and saw the whole place blazing with fire; and trembling came over me, and I begged my guide's help again.* *He stretched out his hand as before and said: “Higher still we must climb.”*

*And at once we were lifted from there and found ourselves above a third heaven.* *This heaven is not as the one that appears to us here; it is firm and solid, and has a level surface spread wide, as though you were to think a sheet of gold laid over it.* *Here again, straight away in the entrance, we found three crosses, scattering a light like lightning, more august both in size and in appearance than all we had seen before.* *And my guide dared to go into the middle of the fire and venerated the crosses; and since I could not do that, I venerated them from where I stood, and passed on.*

**38.** *When we had gone a long way forward, we came to another veil, hung like lightning spread wide through the air; and when we had been carried up to it and had gone in, we found there a great gathering of the powers of heaven, praising and glorifying God.*

*We passed on further still, and another veil opened, of fine linen and purple, of a beauty past explaining.* *From there we came to a place utterly full of glory, where there was a wonderful veil, like amber, most shining and most bright; and a hand of fire drew it back and made our entry ready.*

*There one could see a countless multitude of young men, whose dignity of body, whose fiery colour, whose faces outshining the sun, made them a great sight to see.* *They stood in a very high place, in beautiful order, in the strength of an ageless and bodiless youth, carrying a noble sceptre in their hands; and on this side and on that, legions whose number could not be reckoned.*

*Then my guide spoke to me and said: “See, when this veil is taken away, you will look on the Son of Man, seated at the right hand of the Father; therefore you shall fall down and worship him, and turning your whole mind to him you shall take in, with attentive ears, what he is going to say to you.”*

*Instructed by my guide with these orders, I fixed the sharpness of my eyes on that beautiful veil, and saw a dove of great size flying down to it from above.* *Its head was gold in colour, its breast purple, its wings bright as flames, its feet its own and natural; and rays of light came out of its eyes.* *And while I was gazing more closely at its beautiful form, all at once it went up out of sight.*

**39.** *So when the veil had been taken away, I looked up into that measureless height, fearful to anyone who looks at it, and I saw a throne, surpassing and lifted high, hanging in the air with nothing to hold it up; and from it there stood off a flame, not the kind that comes from fire, but one far surpassing snow in whiteness.*

*On the throne sat my Lord Jesus Christ, clothed in purple and fine linen.* *And when, for the sake of my littleness and weakness, he had drawn in his surpassing splendour for a moment, I looked upon the beauty and the surpassing dignity of that divine humanity of his — the way a man looks at the sun as it scatters its rays most pleasantly at first rising; and after that it was not given to me to enjoy the clear sight of him.*

*So with the veil gone I fell down in that wonderful air and worshipped the Lord three times, and I tried to stay where I was and to look again on his dignity.* *But, as I said before, because of the horror past explaining and the fear beyond compare which that measureless light struck into me as it ringed the throne, I was seized by trembling and by joy together, and I could look no further, nor strain my eyes into the fiery brightness of that all-powerful Godhead.*

*Then a voice was sent out of that light with so great a sound that the whole of that wonderful region of the air trembled, and it came down to my ears; and yet it was gentle in its speech, mild, and sweeter than honey.* *And it uttered three divine words, which I both knew most beautifully and delighted in, in my spirit, more than at any other time.*

*Not long after, another three words were sent out in the same way, and slipping most sweetly into my soul they filled it with a gladness more than human.* *A little while later, another three words rang out; and at once, with a great voice, those venerable armies of the holy angels sang praises to God.* *And though they never hold back from offering praise to God, I understood, when I had considered it, that they had sung that choice and welcome harmony for my sake, and for the singular providence of the Lord Jesus Christ towards me.*

**40.** *When I had heard these words past explaining, at once I came down again the same way I had gone up; and I found myself, given back to myself in every part, standing in that place from which I had been taken up before, turning over in my mind what had happened to me, and where I was now, and where I had just been.*

*And while I wondered greatly how I had come back to the level ground of that divine garden, and looked at everything that was there, I thought and asked myself whether any other man was in this place too, or whether I was alone.*

*Meanwhile I saw an open field in the middle of it, with no plants set in it; and yet it was very beautiful, thick with grass, filled with violets and lilies and roses and countless other flowers.* *Nor did it want the delight of springs, which bubbled up at small intervals with milk and honey and leapt to the height of a single cubit; and such a fragrance and such a sweetness came out of them that what to call that milk and honey, or what to compare them to, I simply do not know.*

*And while I was considering the delight of that place and its greenness fit for rest, and marvelling at the wonderful works of God, and carrying my mind from one beauty to another, there presented himself to my sight a man wrapped about in a shining garment, glowing red like a bright cloud, and carrying a cross.* *And when he had come nearer to me he said:*

*“The crucified Lord our Jesus Christ be with you. Blessed are the fools for Christ's sake, for a wisdom all their own sets them above the rest. God has indeed set you here; but nevertheless go back to the world, where the thistles and the vipers and the serpents and the dragons are, to suffer temptations and goadings.*

*“And I must bring out for you this unheard-of wonder: that no man has ever been in this place, except that one who laboured in the Gospel more than the rest, and you — you who have struggled up to the highest peak of perfection, and have arrived here for the sake of your utter poverty; for that word thrown at you by the beggars, 'Get out of here, dog, and bad luck to you'; for your humility; and last of all because, naked, a boy, a fool, you went down into the arena to close with the prince of this world, and beat him in single combat, and threw him down headlong from the height, and broke his throne in utter confusion.*

**41.** *“So it has fallen to you to look on the wonders of this place, to know the true delights and the reward of the righteous, to walk through the paradise of Christ, and to see him himself here present.* *For it is plain to me that you have seen and have marvelled.* *Now then, what does the foolish world say to all this?* *What do you say?* *Do you see the glory? — Indeed I do.* *Do you look on the beauty? — I do.* *See then, poor despised little man, of how great joys sinners rob themselves, and of their own free will.* *And yet who ever showed them these good things?”*

*As he said this, and looked at me, that most shining man was leaping with a gladness beyond the common, and he went on with what he had begun to say: “And what of this — that the venerable Queen of heaven, more splendid than all the powers above, is not here?* *For she is at this moment down in the wretched world, to bring help and succour to mortal men, having heard the prayers of those who have received the only-begotten Son and Word of God.* *It would not be out of place, then, for me to show you her dwelling, which is more shining than words can explain; but the time does not allow it, dearest friend, for you must go back to the place you came from: so the Lord has commanded.”*

*While he was still saying this I was taken as it were by a sweet sleep; and when I had spent a whole night, as I supposed, sleeping from evening until morning, I found myself at last, as you see, here.*
*And so, my friend, beloved of God, I would have you be glad now, and work hard at it with me, that having obtained salvation we may find that eternal rest there.*

At these words of the saint my own mind was caught up into ecstasy, and I saw a strange and wonderful sight: as an extraordinary fragrance of lilies and roses was being poured out around us, so also certain vapours were rising; and there were present, as I at least believe, holy angels, who while we talked together were burning incense unseen.

After that I begged the saint many times over, as a suppliant, to share with me even one of the words he had heard from the Lord Jesus. But I could not persuade him at all. How that was, or for what reason, I do not know; and I leave it to God and to that blessed mind of his to see to.
